correctness.rationale: Debarre–Manivel require δ⁻=min(δ,n−2k−r)>0 for the connected smooth nonempty scheme in expected dimension. Their strict-positivity equivalence away from a single quadric applies here. In the quadric case δ=1 gives (k+1)(2n−3k−2)=2, so k=1,n=3, excluded and correctly known to have two rulings. Hiep's formula, equivalently Grassmannian adjunction, gives g=1+Be/2 with e>0. With q=k+1 and R_i=binom(d_i+k,k), the expected-dimension identity gives qB=Σ(d_i−1)R_i−q²−1. For r≥3 the sum is at least 3q(q+1)/2≥(q+1)², with equality only at q=2, three equations, all quadrics. For r=2, two quadrics give 1+ΣR_i≡1 mod q and are inadmissible. One cubic or larger gives the lower bound q(q+1)(2q+7)/6>(q+1)². A single degree ≥3 for q≥3 gives q(q+1)(q+2)/3>(q+1)². At q=2 a hypersurface has even degree by divisibility, and hence after the quadric exclusion d≥4, giving d²−1>9. Equality therefore forces k=1,n=6 and the three quadrics. Independently, on Gr(2,7) the Plücker degree is the coefficient of x⁶y⁵ in (x−y)(x+y)[4xy(x+y)]³, namely 64(6−4)=128, giving g=129. This also confirms unique distance g−e=1 and no genus-zero or genus-one case in the stated range. The bundled script was inspected, not executed; its finite grid and fixed degree calibrations are not the proof.

value.rationale: For naturally polarized moduli curves in Grassmannians, this gives a sharp universal lower bound on the canonical-to-Plücker ratio and locates the only extremal complete-intersection type. It excludes rational and elliptic curves in this family and distinguishes the three-quadric curve from all other admissible families, rather than merely recomputing its known genus.
